text:
ashley: Customer on prod-uk reports 10-20% of requests routed to us-west which causes 600+ms p99 and intermittent 401s. Billing shows duplicate charge attempts from retries.

ashley: Repro steps from customer: curl to api.redwood.ai with region=eu header, 3/10 still land in us-west. They provided trace IDs.

ashley: Attaching one example trace id: trace=txn_0a9f3b. From logs we see X-Region-Hint: eu-west and upstream-route chosen us-west-2.

samir: Can you paste the raw headers and the gateway trace? suspecting L7 route selection fallback when checksum mismatch occurs.

ashley: Paste of request headers:
```
:authority: api.redwood.ai
x-region-hint: eu-west
x-client-id: cust-342
authorization: Bearer ****
user-agent: curl/7.68.0
```
Gateway decision log (excerpt):
```
[2026-02-18T11:22:09Z] route_select: policy=region_preference, candidate_pool=[eu-pool, global-pool]
[2026-02-18T11:22:09Z] checksum_mismatch: route_key=eu-pool, expected=0x1f4a, actual=0x1f4b
[2026-02-18T11:22:09Z] fallback_to: us-west-2
```

ashley: Customer also saw increased token billing during these events due to client retries on 401.

irene: ops-bot, can you surface recent config pushes to envoys that might change route key generation or header normalization?

ops-bot: deploybot: recent rollouts:
- 2026-02-17 03:14 UTC - eng-runtime: l7-routing-hash-fix (canary)
- 2026-02-17 07:50 UTC - infra: envoy-1.25.3 patch (global)

samir: That l7-routing-hash-fix is suspicious. It changed header canonicalization for route hashing to use lowercased header names, but some pools still compute checksums with legacy case-sensitive code. Could cause key mismatch and fallback.

samir: Quick repro I ran: repeated curl with mixed-case X-Region-Hint sometimes matches old pool key, sometimes new -> results in TTL drift and sticky session loss.

ashley: Customer confirms they set header with mixed-case from their client lib. They only observed issue after Feb 17.

irene: Impact assessment: looks like customers with non-normalized region hints in headers + mixed pool versions will see 5-15% cross-region misroutes and auth failures when fallback path uses a different auth token provider.

irene: Action items:
- samir -> hotfix to make route key computation backward-compatible and add header normalization at edge (PR + canary)
- infra -> roll back envoy patch on a couple nodes to reproduce and compare (ticket created)
- support -> identify customers with retries/duplicate billing and offer credits (ashley)

samir: Draft patch: normalize headers to lowercase before hashing and treat missing header canonicalization as equivalent. Adding test vectors. Pushing PR in 30m.

ashley: Telling customer we have a suspected root cause and will patch; asked for list of traceIDs and example requests, got 7 more.

irene: Also recommend short-term mitigation: add an L7 rule to prefer pools by metadata tag region=hint if header present (bypass checksum) until fully rolled out.

samir: I'll coordinate rollback of canary if needed. If everyone agrees, I can land patch and request infra to rollout canary to 10% first.

ashley: Thanks — I'll file the billing follow-ups and notify affected customers. cc @samir @irene :thumbsup:

samir: landing patch now, will post updates in this thread with CI + canary metrics.

ops-bot: alert: canary-deploy started at 2026-02-18T12:05:00Z for l7-routing-hash-fix-hotfix (10% nodes)

samir: canary metrics after 20m: misroute rate down from ~8% -> 0.6% on canary nodes. Rolling to 100% in progress.

ashley: Customer confirms routes stabilized after 25m. Marking support ticket as mitigated; will follow up for credits.

irene: Postmortem: schedule config compatibility checks in CI for header canonicalization changes and add a metric for checksum_mismatch events to alert earlier.

ashley: Closing loop with customer and updating internal KB with repro steps/code snippet to normalize header casing.
